# Capacity, scaling laws and cost {#sec-capacity}

*Before this chapter:* the metric and the scoring protocol (@sec-metrics, @sec-protocol), the
reference configurations and the study configurations (@sec-study-configurations), and ISLA's
quadrature (@sec-isla-quadrature). No result of the dataset chapters is assumed.

**Training cells per case stop paying above 100,000, the error falls toward a floor as the model
and the training set grow, a fitted law says how to split a compute budget between the two, and
the cost of a training step is linear in the number of tokens.** This chapter answers the three questions an engineer asks before spending a
GPU budget on a surrogate: how many cells per case, how many parameters against how many training
cases, and what a step costs. All three are measured on the DrivAerML Surface task, the one
dataset with a ladder in every direction, and the scaling law is checked on HiLiftAeroML.

The studies behind the answers ran on smaller ISLAs than the reference configuration (ISLA width
512, 12 layers, 512 slices, learning rate 3.75e-4, 200,000 training cells, with the normalized
slice reads). Each figure and table names its instrument in its caption, in the form defined in
@sec-study-configurations, and is read for slopes, floors and mechanisms, never as a standing.
Where the data allow, the three reference configurations (GeoTransolver width 256 at 1e-3 and
200,000 cells; Transolver width 512, 16 layers, at 1e-3 and 100,000 cells) are drawn on the same
axes as stars, marked as the different instrument they are. Every error is the area-weighted
relative L2 of surface pressure, scored in float32 at 200,000 cells per case on the 48 DrivAerML
validation cars or the 180 HiLiftAeroML validation wings; every ratio is baseline ÷ ISLA.

```{python}
#| label: setup-capacity
#| include: false
import sys; sys.path.insert(0, ".")
from palette import *
import standing as S
import json, statistics
from pathlib import Path
RES = Path("..") / "results"
J = lambda p: json.load(open(RES / p))
mean = statistics.mean
ISOJ = J("isocost_reduction_2026-09-20.json"); ISO = ISOJ["configurations"]
QV = J("quadvar_reduction_2026-09-17.json")["arms"]          # stratified and uniform draws of 10,000-cell-trained checkpoints
P2 = J("p200k_trio_reduction_2026-09-19.json")                 # the same three architectures trained at 200,000 cells
SHL = J("scalehl_2026-09-26.json")
SLD = J("scalelaw_2026-10-08.json"); SL = SLD["configurations"]; SLF = SLD["fits"]
COST = J("char/char_lanes_cost_2026-10-04.json")["cost"]       # the reference configurations' training cost, four GB300 ranks
import statistics as st
CS = J("cost_sweep_ref_gb300_bf16_2026-09-22.json")["runs"]    # the one-GPU cost sweep
at = lambda arm, tok: next(r for r in CS if r["arm"] == arm and r["tokens"] == tok and r["status"] == "ok")
SURF = S.Standing("drivaerml_surface"); HLS = S.Standing("hilift")
REF_KEYS = (("ISLA", "isla_ref"), ("GeoTransolver", "gt"), ("Transolver", "t"))
def ref_point(stand, task, arch, f="pressure_l2"):
    """(parameters, seed-mean error) of one reference configuration on one task."""
    return COST[task][arch]["n_parameters"], stand.err(arch, f)
def star(ax, x, y, key, label=None, ms=15, **kw):
    """A reference configuration: the architecture's color, a black-edged star."""
    return ax.plot([x], [y], marker="*", ms=ms, mfc=STYLE[key]["color"], mec=INK, mew=0.9, ls="none",
                   label=label, zorder=6, **kw)
HL_NOTE = ("" if S.DATASETS["hilift"].reference or not S.DATASETS["hilift"].fair_drive else
           " HiLiftAeroML's ISLA star is from checkpoints of the raw-read variant (@sec-isla-layer), not of the reference configuration.")
```

## Cells per case saturate above 100,000 {#sec-equal-budget}

**Above 100,000 training cells per case the error of every architecture is flat in the cell
count, and doubling the training length moves it by less than a seed spread, so neither cells
nor epochs buys accuracy past the reporting protocol.** A training cell is a quadrature node: the
model sees a random subsample of the surface mesh each step, and its sums over that subsample
estimate integrals over the surface. Once the estimate is good enough that the network's own
approximation error dominates, more nodes buy nothing. @tbl-cells-ladder measures where that
happens. Each row trains one model at one width from 100,000 to 600,000 cells per case and scores
every run on the same instrument (200,000 cells, float32), so the only variable down a column is
how densely the training draw samples the surface.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-cells-ladder
#| output: asis
ladder = [("ISLA, 192 wide, 1e-3", "isla", 192, "1e-3", (100, 200, 400, 600)),
          ("ISLA, 384 wide, 5e-4", "isla", 384, "5e-4", (100, 200, 400)),
          ("ISLA, 512 wide, 3.75e-4", "isla", 512, "3.75e-4", (200, 300)),
          ("GeoTransolver, 256 wide, 3e-3", "gt_unit", 256, "3e-3", (100, 200, 400)),
          ("Transolver, 256 wide, 3e-3", "transolver_unit", 256, "3e-3", (100, 200, 400))]
out = "| architecture, width, learning rate | training cells per case | error, seed 42 / 43 | mean | ÷ the same model at its smallest count |\n|---|--:|---|--:|--:|\n"
for lab, m, w, lr, cells in ladder:
    base = ISO[f"{m}|w{w}|c{cells[0]}k|lr{lr}|ep500"]["pressure_l2_mean"]
    for n in cells:
        c = ISO[f"{m}|w{w}|c{n}k|lr{lr}|ep500"]
        s = " / ".join(f"{v:.4f}" for v in c["pressure_l2_seeds"])
        out += f"| {lab} | {n},000 | {s} | **{c['pressure_l2_mean']:.4f}** | {c['pressure_l2_mean'] / base:.3f} |\n"
spread = max(abs(ISO[f"{m}|w{w}|c{n}k|lr{lr}|ep500"]["pressure_l2_mean"] / ISO[f"{m}|w{w}|c{cs[0]}k|lr{lr}|ep500"]["pressure_l2_mean"] - 1)
             for _, m, w, lr, cs in ladder for n in cs)
print(out)
print(": The cell-count ladder on the DrivAerML Surface task: 435 training cars, 500 epochs, two seeds, surface-pressure error on the 48 "
      "validation cars, scored in float32 at 200,000 cells whatever the training count. *Instrument:* ISLA at 192, 384 and 512 wide, 256 slices, "
      "1e-3, 5e-4 and 3.75e-4, raw slice reads (@sec-study-configurations); GeoTransolver and Transolver at 256 wide and 3e-3. "
      f"How to read this: a within-model control of the training cell count. No row moves by more than {100 * spread:.1f}% from its model's "
      "smallest count, so above 100,000 cells the count is not an axis of accuracy for any of the three. It is not a comparison between "
      "architectures: the rows differ in width and parameters. Data: results/isocost_reduction_2026-09-20.json.")
```

```{python}
#| label: para-epochs
#| output: asis
ep = lambda k: abs(ISO[k.replace("ep500", "ep1000")]["pressure_l2_mean"] / ISO[k]["pressure_l2_mean"] - 1) * 100
print(f"The fitted exponent of error against training cells is {abs(ISOJ['bars']['cells_exponent']['alpha_isla']):.2f} for ISLA and "
      f"{ISOJ['bars']['cells_exponent']['alpha_gt']:.2f} for GeoTransolver over this range. The training length is converged too: "
      f"1,000 epochs instead of 500 at 200,000 cells move ISLA at 192 wide by {ep('isla|w192|c200k|lr1e-3|ep500'):.2f}% and GeoTransolver "
      f"at 256 wide by {ep('gt_unit|w256|c200k|lr3e-3|ep500'):.2f}%. What still buys accuracy at 435 cars is capacity "
      "(@sec-shared-floor) and, more cheaply, cases (@sec-compute-allocation).")
```

### Below 100,000 cells ISLA pays a quadrature-noise penalty {#sec-deficit-anatomy}

**Below the saturation count the cell count still pays, and it pays ISLA more than the baselines,
because ISLA's slice states are measure-weighted quadratures whose variance a sparse draw
inflates.** Each slice state is a ratio estimator of a surface integral (@sec-isla-quadrature):

$$
Z_s \;=\; \sum_i a_{is}\, \tilde h_i \;=\; \frac{\sum_i w_i\, e^{\lambda_{is}}\, \tilde h_i}{\sum_i w_i\, e^{\lambda_{is}}},
$$

with $a_{is}$ the routing weight of token $i$ into slice $s$, which carries the token's measure
weight $w_i$ (@sec-isla-quadrature), $\lambda_{is}$ its learned routing score and $\tilde h_i$ its
normalized state. Under an independent draw of $n$ cells its variance falls like
$1/n_\text{eff}$, where Kish's effective sample size $n_\text{eff} = (\sum_i w_i)^2 / \sum_i
w_i^2$ is smaller than $n$ whenever the cell areas vary. A surface mesh refined at the edges and
coarse on the flanks has cell areas spread over orders of magnitude, so a weighted mean over
10,000 such cells is noisier than an unweighted one. The baselines average token states without
weights; they pay a different price, a bias toward wherever the mesher put its cells
(@sec-sampling-laws), but not this variance.

Two scorings of the same checkpoints separate the variance from everything else
(@fig-quadrature-noise). A stratified draw of 10,000 cells (a systematic sample along a
space-filling curve, which keeps every cell's inclusion probability and only spreads the cells
evenly) leaves the integrand alone and lowers the variance. An independent draw of 40,000 cells
lowers it by adding nodes. If the penalty is quadrature variance, both should lower ISLA's error
more than the baselines'.

```{python}
#| label: fig-quadrature-noise
#| fig-cap: >
#|   Surface-pressure error of checkpoints trained at 10,000 cells per case, scored at 10,000,
#|   20,000 and 40,000 cells per case by an independent uniform draw (filled marks, joined) and at
#|   10,000 and 20,000 cells by a stratified draw of the same inclusion law (open marks), on the
#|   DrivAerML Surface task (435 training cars, 48 validation cars, float32, two seeds; seed means,
#|   the stratified seeds as short bars). *Instrument:* ISLA at 192 wide, 256 slices, 1e-3, raw
#|   slice reads (@sec-study-configurations); GeoTransolver and Transolver at 256 wide. How to read
#|   this: the drop from a filled to an open mark at the same count is variance removed without
#|   adding a node; ISLA's drop is the largest, and so is its gain from 10,000 to 40,000 cells. The
#|   figure says nothing about models trained at the reporting protocol, where the penalty is gone
#|   (@tbl-cells-ladder). Data: results/quadvar_reduction_2026-09-17.json.
#| fig-alt: "Error against scoring cell count for three architectures; ISLA's uniform-draw curve falls most steeply, and its stratified point at 10,000 cells sits well below its uniform point."
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.4, 4.4))
for arm, key, dx in (("isla_ref", "isla_ref", 0.9), ("gt_unit", "gt", 1.0), ("transolver_unit", "t", 1.11)):
    q = QV[arm]; ns = sorted(int(k) for k in q["unif"])
    kw = series_kwargs(key, ms=7, lw=1.8, label="_nolegend_")
    ax.plot([n * dx for n in ns], [q["unif"][str(n)] for n in ns], **kw)
    sn = sorted(int(k) for k in q["strat"])
    ax.plot([n * dx for n in sn], [q["strat"][str(n)]["mean"] for n in sn], ls="none", marker=STYLE[key]["marker"],
            mfc="white", mec=STYLE[key]["color"], mew=1.8, ms=8)
    for n in sn:
        ax.plot([n * dx] * 2, q["strat"][str(n)]["seeds"], color=STYLE[key]["color"], lw=1.0, alpha=0.6)
    label_line(ax, ns[-1] * dx * 1.07, q["unif"][str(ns[-1])], STYLE[key]["label"], STYLE[key]["color"])
ax.plot([], [], ls="none", marker="s", mfc="white", mec=INK2, mew=1.5, label="stratified draw, same law")
ax.set_xscale("log"); ax.set_xticks([10000, 20000, 40000]); ax.set_xticklabels(["10,000", "20,000", "40,000"])
ax.xaxis.set_minor_locator(mpl.ticker.NullLocator()); ax.set_xlim(8500, 66000)
ax.set_xlabel("scoring cells per case [count]"); ax.set_ylabel("surface-pressure error,\narea-weighted relative L2 [–]")
ax.legend(loc="upper right", fontsize=8.2)
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()
```

```{python}
#| label: para-quadrature-noise
#| output: asis
gain = lambda a: 100 * (1 - QV[a]["strat"]["10000"]["mean"] / QV[a]["unif"]["10000"])
dens = lambda a: 100 * (1 - QV[a]["unif"]["40000"] / QV[a]["unif"]["10000"])
T = P2["tenk_reference"]; A = P2["arms"]
gt200 = min(A["gt_unit_lr1e3"]["pressure_mean"], A["gt_unit_lr3e3"]["pressure_mean"])
print(f"The stratified draw lowers ISLA's error by {gain('isla_ref'):.1f}%, GeoTransolver's by {gain('gt_unit'):.1f}% and Transolver's by "
      f"{gain('transolver_unit'):.1f}%; quadrupling the independent draw lowers them by {dens('isla_ref'):.1f}%, {dens('gt_unit'):.1f}% and "
      f"{dens('transolver_unit'):.1f}%. The same penalty shows in training. Trained and scored at 10,000 cells, GeoTransolver ÷ ISLA is "
      f"{T['gt_unit'] / T['isla']:.2f}; trained and scored at 200,000 cells, the same pair of architectures reads {gt200 / A['isla']['pressure_mean']:.2f}. "
      "The deficit at the small count is a sampling cost of the quadrature, not a property of the operator, and it is gone by 100,000 cells. "
      "For deployment at a small budget the consequence is practical: use the stratified sampler, or more cells (@sec-using-sampler). "
      "Data: results/quadvar_reduction_2026-09-17.json; results/p200k_trio_reduction_2026-09-19.json.")
```

## The capacity floor {#sec-shared-floor}

**At 435 DrivAerML cars and 100,000 cells per case both architectures approach the same floor in
surface-pressure error as width and depth grow, and they reach it at similar parameter counts.** With cells saturated, what remains at a fixed dataset is capacity.
Two ladders measure it. A width ladder takes ISLA from 192 to 1,536 wide and GeoTransolver from
256 to 2,048 wide, each width at the better of the learning rates run for it. A depth ladder takes
ISLA at 384 wide from 12 to 48 layers and GeoTransolver at 512 wide from 12 to 24. Every run
trains for 500 epochs with two seeds. @fig-capacity puts every run on one axis of trainable
parameters, with the three reference configurations beside them.

```{python}
#| label: setup-floor
#| include: false
CAPI = J("cap435_interim_2026-09-20.json")["configurations"]
CFG = J("cap435_reduction_2026-09-20.json")["configurations"]
RNC = J("routenorm_interim_2026-09-20.json")["configurations"]
EXT = J("routenorm_extension_2026-09-21.json")["configurations"]
RP = J("routenorm_p200k_2026-09-22.json")["configurations"]
PW = {c["width"]: c["params"] for c in CFG.values() if c["model"] == "isla" and c["depth"] == 12 and c["slices"] == 256}
def best_of(cands):
    """(params, mean, seeds) of the lowest-error candidate; candidates are (mean, seeds, params)."""
    m, s, p = min(cands, key=lambda t: t[0]); return p, m, s
def isla_w(w):
    cands = [(c["mean"], c["seeds"], PW[w]) for k, c in RNC.items() if k.startswith(f"cars|cos|w{w}|")]
    cands += [(c["pressure_l2_mean"], c["pressure_l2_seeds"], c["params"]) for k, c in EXT.items() if k.startswith(f"isla|cos|w{w}|d12|")]
    return best_of(cands)
def isla_d(key):
    c = EXT[key]; return c["params"], c["pressure_l2_mean"], c["pressure_l2_seeds"]
def gt_w(w):
    cands = [(c["pressure_l2_mean"], c["pressure_l2_seeds"], c["params"]) for c in CFG.values() if c["model"] == "gt" and c["width"] == w and c["depth"] == 12]
    cands += [(c["pressure_l2_mean"], c["pressure_l2_seeds"], c["params"]) for k, c in EXT.items() if k.startswith(f"gt|w{w}|d12|")]
    return best_of(cands)
gt_width = [gt_w(w) for w in (256, 512, 1024, 2048)]
c24 = CFG["gt|w512|d24|s256|lr3e-3"]
gt_depth = [gt_w(512), (c24["params"], c24["pressure_l2_mean"], c24["pressure_l2_seeds"])]
isla_width = [isla_w(w) for w in (192, 384, 768, 1024, 1536)]
isla_depth = [isla_w(384), isla_d("isla|cos|w384|d24|lr5e-4"), isla_d("isla|cos|w384|d48|lr2.5e-4")]
p200 = RP["cars|cos|w384|d24|lr5e-4|c200k"]
isla_200k = (EXT["isla|cos|w384|d24|lr5e-4"]["params"], p200["pressure_l2_mean"], p200["pressure_l2_seeds"])
FLOOR = sorted(s[1] for s in isla_width + isla_depth)[:2] + sorted(s[1] for s in gt_width + gt_depth)[:2]
floor_lo, floor_hi = min(FLOOR), max(FLOOR)
REFP = {a: ref_point(SURF, "DrivAerML Surface", a) for a, _ in REF_KEYS}
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-capacity
#| fig-cap: >
#|   Surface-pressure error against trainable parameters on the DrivAerML Surface task (435
#|   training cars, 100,000 training cells per case unless labeled, 500 epochs, float32 at 200,000
#|   cells on the 48 validation cars; two-seed means with the seeds as short bars). Red:
#|   GeoTransolver's width ladder at 12 layers (filled circles) and its 24-layer run at 512 wide
#|   (open circle). Blue: ISLA's width ladder at 12 layers (filled squares), its depth ladder at 384
#|   wide (open diamonds, dotted), and the 24-layer run trained at 200,000 cells (cross, drawn
#|   offset to the right of its 100,000-cell twin, which has the same parameters).
#|   *Instrument:* ISLA at 192 to 1,536 wide, 256 slices, 1e-3 to 2.5e-4, raw slice reads
#|   (@sec-study-configurations). Large black-edged stars: the three reference configurations on the
#|   same validation cars, a different instrument (200,000 training cells, 100,000 for Transolver;
#|   the normalized slice reads and 512 slices for ISLA; results/char/drivaerml_surface_a2.json,
#|   parameters from results/char/char_lanes_cost_2026-10-04.json). The gray band spans the best two
#|   ladder runs of each architecture. How to read this: the x axis is parameters, not memory or
#|   time (those are @tbl-ref-cost and @fig-cost-sweep); GeoTransolver-2,048's count is extrapolated
#|   from its measured 256 to 1,024 ladder; the y axis starts below the floor. Data:
#|   results/cap435_reduction_2026-09-20.json, results/routenorm_interim_2026-09-20.json,
#|   results/routenorm_extension_2026-09-21.json, results/routenorm_p200k_2026-09-22.json.
#| fig-alt: "Scatter of validation pressure error against parameter count on a log axis; ISLA's width and depth ladders in blue and GeoTransolver's in red converge into a gray band near 0.040, and three stars for the reference configurations sit above the band."
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8.6, 5.4))
def draw(series, key, label, ls="-", marker=None, mfc=None, ms=7):
    kw = series_kwargs(key, lw=1.8, ms=ms); kw["ls"] = ls; kw["label"] = label
    if marker: kw["marker"] = marker
    if mfc is not None: kw["mfc"] = mfc
    ax.plot([s[0] for s in series], [s[1] for s in series], **kw, zorder=3)
    for x, _, seeds in series:
        ax.plot([x] * len(seeds), seeds, ls="none", marker="_", color=kw["color"], ms=8, mew=1.1, zorder=4)
draw(gt_width, "gt", "GeoTransolver, width 256 → 2,048")
draw(gt_depth, "gt", "GeoTransolver, 512 wide, 12 → 24 layers", ls=":", mfc="white")
draw(isla_width, "isla_ref", "ISLA, width 192 → 1,536")
draw(isla_depth, "isla_ref", "ISLA, 384 wide, 12 → 48 layers", ls=":", marker="D", mfc="white")
draw([(isla_200k[0] * 1.12,) + isla_200k[1:]], "isla_ref", "ISLA, 384 × 24, trained at 200,000 cells (drawn offset right)", ls="none", marker="X", ms=10)
for a, key in REF_KEYS:
    star(ax, *REFP[a], key, ms=17)
    ax.annotate(f"{a} reference\n(different instrument)", REFP[a], textcoords="offset points", xytext=(9, 4), fontsize=8.0,
                color=STYLE[key]["color"], path_effects=halo())
ax.axhspan(floor_lo, floor_hi, color=GRID, zorder=0)
ax.text(5.6e6, (floor_lo + floor_hi) / 2, f"floor band {floor_lo:.4f} to {floor_hi:.4f}", fontsize=8.5, color=INK2, va="center", path_effects=halo())
ax.set_xscale("log"); ax.set_xlim(5e6, 1.0e9); ax.set_ylim(0.039, 0.0485)
ax.set_xlabel("trainable parameters [count]"); ax.set_ylabel("surface-pressure error,\narea-weighted relative L2 [–]")
ax.set_xticks([1e7, 2e7, 5e7, 1e8, 2e8, 5e8, 1e9]); ax.set_xticklabels(["10M", "20M", "50M", "100M", "200M", "500M", "1B"])
ax.xaxis.set_minor_formatter(mpl.ticker.NullFormatter())
ax.legend(loc="upper right", fontsize=8.0)
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()
```

```{python}
#| label: para-capacity-readings
#| output: asis
gains = " / ".join(f"{100 * (1 - b[1] / a[1]):.1f}%" for a, b in zip(gt_width[:-1], gt_width[1:]))
ref_over = {a: REFP[a][1] / floor_hi for a, _ in REF_KEYS}
print(f"1. **Width pays both architectures at first, and only GeoTransolver keeps buying with it.** GeoTransolver's width ladder improves by "
      f"{gains} per doubling from 256 to 2,048 wide, the last doubling the size of a seed spread. ISLA's improves by "
      f"{100 * (1 - isla_width[1][1] / isla_width[0][1]):.1f}% from 192 to 384 wide and then levels off: 768 wide gains a further "
      f"{100 * (1 - isla_width[2][1] / isla_width[1][1]):.1f}%, and the 1,024- and 1,536-wide runs are worse than the 384-wide one "
      f"({isla_width[3][1]:.4f} and {isla_width[4][1]:.4f} against {isla_width[1][1]:.4f}).")
print(f"2. **Depth is ISLA's capacity axis on this dataset.** At 384 wide, 24 layers read {isla_depth[1][1]:.4f} at "
      f"{isla_depth[1][0] / 1e6:.0f}M parameters and 48 layers {isla_depth[2][1]:.4f} at {isla_depth[2][0] / 1e6:.0f}M. The 24-layer run "
      f"trained at 200,000 cells reads {isla_200k[1]:.4f}, within {100 * abs(isla_200k[1] / isla_depth[1][1] - 1):.1f}% of its 100,000-cell twin, "
      "so the floor is not an artifact of the 100,000-cell budget.")
print(f"3. **Both reach one floor at similar parameter counts.** GeoTransolver at 512 × 24 reads {gt_depth[1][1]:.4f} at "
      f"{gt_depth[1][0] / 1e6:.0f}M parameters and ISLA at 384 × 24 {isla_depth[1][1]:.4f} at {isla_depth[1][0] / 1e6:.0f}M; at 12 layers "
      f"GeoTransolver at 512 wide reads {gt_width[1][1]:.4f} at {gt_width[1][0] / 1e6:.0f}M and ISLA at 384 wide {isla_width[1][1]:.4f} at "
      f"{isla_width[1][0] / 1e6:.0f}M; the pairs differ by {100 * max(abs(gt_depth[1][1] / isla_depth[1][1] - 1), abs(gt_width[1][1] / isla_width[1][1] - 1)):.1f}% or less. At about {gt_width[2][0] / 1e6:.0f}M parameters GeoTransolver at "
      f"1,024 wide ÷ ISLA at 384 × 48 = {gt_width[2][1] / isla_depth[2][1]:.3f}.")
print(f"4. **The reference configurations sit above the band.** Their errors are "
      + ", ".join(f"{a} {REFP[a][1]:.4f} at {REFP[a][0] / 1e6:.0f}M parameters ({ref_over[a]:.2f}× the band's upper edge)" for a, _ in REF_KEYS)
      + ". They are a different instrument (more training cells and, for ISLA, 512 slices and the normalized reads), "
        "chosen under a memory budget of 80 GiB per GPU rather than for capacity. Whether the reference ISLA reaches the band is "
        "an open question (@sec-oq-scaling).")
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-floor
#| output: asis
def rec(mean_, seeds, params, mem=None, est=False):
    return dict(pressure_l2_mean=mean_, pressure_l2_seeds=seeds, params=params, peak_mem_gb=mem, params_estimated=est)
c384 = RNC["cars|cos|w384|lr5e-4"]
floor_rows = [
    ("ISLA", "384 × 12", "100,000", "5e-4", rec(c384["mean"], c384["seeds"], PW[384])),
    ("ISLA", "384 × 24", "100,000", "5e-4", EXT["isla|cos|w384|d24|lr5e-4"]),
    ("ISLA", "384 × 24", "200,000", "5e-4", rec(p200["pressure_l2_mean"], p200["pressure_l2_seeds"], EXT["isla|cos|w384|d24|lr5e-4"]["params"])),
    ("ISLA", "384 × 48", "100,000", "2.5e-4", EXT["isla|cos|w384|d48|lr2.5e-4"]),
    ("GeoTransolver", "512 × 12", "200,000", "3e-3", ISO["gt_unit|w512|c200k|lr3e-3|ep500"]),
    ("GeoTransolver", "512 × 24", "100,000", "3e-3", CAPI["gt|w512|d24|s256|lr3e-3"]),
    ("GeoTransolver", "1,024 × 12", "100,000", "1e-3", CAPI["gt|w1024|d12|s256|lr1e3"]),
    ("GeoTransolver", "2,048 × 12", "100,000", "1e-3", EXT["gt|w2048|d12|lr1e-3"]),
]
out = "| architecture | width × layers | parameters | training cells | learning rate | error, mean (seeds) | peak reserved memory [GiB] |\n|---|---|--:|--:|--:|---|--:|\n"
for arch, shape, cells, lr, c in floor_rows:
    params = f"{c['params'] / 1e6:.0f}M" + (" (estimated)" if c.get("params_estimated") else "")
    seeds = " / ".join(f"{v:.4f}" for v in c["pressure_l2_seeds"])
    memv = c.get("peak_mem_gb")
    out += f"| {arch} | {shape} | {params} | {cells} | {lr} | **{c['pressure_l2_mean']:.4f}** ({seeds}) | {'not logged' if memv is None else f'{memv:.0f}'} |\n"
print(out)
print(": The ladder runs at or near the floor on the DrivAerML Surface task (435 cars, 500 epochs, two seeds, float32 at 200,000 cells on the "
      "48 validation cars). *Instrument:* ISLA at 384 wide, 256 slices, 5e-4 and 2.5e-4, raw slice reads (@sec-study-configurations). "
      "*Parameters*: trainable, as counted by the training script. *Memory*: the peak of the per-step reserved memory the training log "
      "records, per GPU. How to read this: the table names the floor and what each model pays to reach it; the errors differ by less than "
      "a seed spread, so it is not a ranking. Data: results/isocost_reduction_2026-09-20.json, results/cap435_interim_2026-09-20.json, "

      "results/routenorm_p200k_2026-09-22.json.")
```

## What the reference configurations spend {#sec-review-frontier}

**At their reference configurations the three architectures spend different resources, and a
comparison between them is resource-matched only on the memory budget they were chosen under.**
ISLA's reference has several times GeoTransolver's parameters, and Transolver's trains at half
the cells. @tbl-ref-cost lists, for every task with a cost record, what one training epoch costs
each architecture on four GB300 GPUs, the GPU-hours of a 500-epoch training run, and the headline error
of its standing. Two terms need a line each. The *allocator peak* is the largest amount of GPU
memory the training process held in live tensors at once (PyTorch's `max_memory_allocated`);
the allocator reserves somewhat more in cached blocks, so the peak is a lower bound on the card a
run needs. The *epoch time* is wall clock and includes data loading, so it is the cost a user
pays, not the network's arithmetic alone.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-ref-cost
#| output: asis
TASKS = [("DrivAerML Surface", "drivaerml_surface"), ("DrivAerML Volume", "drivaerml_volume"), ("Shift-SUV", "shift_suv"),
         ("AirfRANS", "airfrans"), ("Tensile2D", "tensile2d"), ("lug", "lug"), ("DeepJEB++", "deepjeb")]
EPOCHS = {"DeepJEB++": 40}  # every other task trains for 500 epochs (@sec-protocol)
lane_gpuh = lambda task, arch: COST[task][arch]["epoch_seconds"] * EPOCHS.get(task, 500) * 4 / 3600
out = "| dataset and task | architecture | parameters | allocator peak per GPU [GiB] | epoch [s] | GPU-hours per run | error, first headline field | ÷ ISLA |\n|---|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|\n"
for task, key in TASKS:
    st_ = S.Standing(key); f = st_.ds.headline[0]
    for i, (arch, _) in enumerate(REF_KEYS):
        c = COST[task][arch]
        name = st_.ds.name if i == 0 else ""
        rel = "" if arch == "ISLA" else f"{st_.ratio(arch, f):.2f}"
        out += (f"| {name} | {arch} | {c['n_parameters'] / 1e6:.1f}M | {c['peak_gib']:.1f} | {c['epoch_seconds']:.0f} | {lane_gpuh(task, arch):.0f} | "
                f"{st_.err(arch, f):.4f} | {rel} |\n")
print(out)
print(": What the three reference configurations spend, per dataset and task: trainable parameters, the training allocator peak per GPU (the "
      "maximum over four GB300 ranks, bfloat16, one case per GPU), the wall time of one training epoch, and the GPU-hours of one training run "
      "(epoch time × epochs × four GPUs; 500 epochs, 40 on DeepJEB++), beside the seed-mean error of the dataset's first headline field from its "
      "standing and the ratio baseline ÷ ISLA. The one-epoch cost runs used the raw slice reads, which have the same parameters and the "
      "same tensors as the normalized reads, so the counts are exact and the costs representative. How to read this: the cost columns come "
      "from one-epoch runs of each configuration and the error "
      "column from the 500-epoch standing, so the table pairs a price with a result; it does not say what each architecture would score at "
      "another architecture's budget. Data: results/char/char_lanes_cost_2026-10-04.json and the standing artifacts of @sec-standing.")
```

## What compute should buy: cases, parameters, epochs {#sec-compute-allocation}

**On the DrivAerML Surface task the error is a floor plus two decaying power laws, one in
training cases and one in parameters, and minimizing that law at fixed training compute puts
most of every new order of magnitude of compute into parameters and the rest into cases.** This is the question a language-model practitioner asks of a surrogate (the
"compute-optimal" or Chinchilla question): with a fixed budget, how large a training set and how
large a model? Epochs are already settled: they are converged at 500 (@sec-equal-budget), so the
budget is spent on cases $n$ and parameters $P$.

The instrument is a scaling study on two surface datasets. ISLA at three widths and GeoTransolver
at three widths train for 500 epochs at 100,000 cells per case on 27, 54, 109, 218 and 435
DrivAerML cars and on 35, 210, 510 and 1,260 HiLiftAeroML wings, two seeds each, scored in
float32. @fig-scaling-cases shows the raw curves. They bend: steep at the small rungs, flattening
toward a floor at the large ones, on both datasets.

```{python}
#| label: fig-scaling-cases
#| fig-cap: >
#|   Surface-pressure error against training cases for three widths of each model on the
#|   DrivAerML Surface task (top; 27 to 435 cars, 48 validation cars) and on HiLiftAeroML
#|   (bottom; 35 to 1,260 wings, 180 validation wings), 500 epochs at 100,000 cells per case,
#|   float32, two-seed means with the seeds as short bars. Lighter shades are narrower models.
#|   Dotted curves: the fitted law of @tbl-scaling-fit at each width, drawn where the fit is
#|   accepted (ISLA on both datasets, GeoTransolver on the wings); gray dashed line: ISLA's fitted
#|   floor. *Instrument:* ISLA at 192, 384 and 768 wide, 256 slices, 1e-3 / 5e-4 / 5e-4, raw slice
#|   reads (@sec-study-configurations); GeoTransolver at 256, 512 and 1,024 wide, 3e-3 / 3e-3 /
#|   1e-3. Black-edged stars: the three reference configurations at the full training set of 435
#|   cars, a different instrument (results/char/drivaerml_surface_a2.json), offset sideways for
#|   legibility; the HiLiftAeroML panel carries them only where its standing compares the
#|   architectures (@sec-oq-unit-direction). How to read this: the
#|   vertical spread between shades is what parameters buy at one training-set size; the slope is
#|   what cases buy. Both axes are logarithmic. Data: results/scalelaw_2026-10-08.json.
#| fig-alt: "Two stacked log-log scatters of pressure error against training cases, DrivAerML above and HiLiftAeroML below; three blue shades for ISLA widths and three red shades for GeoTransolver widths, dotted fitted curves bending toward a floor, and stars for the reference configurations."
def grid(ds):
    """Per model and width, the (n, two-seed mean, seeds) points of one dataset, and the parameter counts."""
    pts = {"isla": {}, "gt": {}}; params = {"isla": {}, "gt": {}}
    for c in SL.values():
        if c["dataset"] == ds and c["pressure_l2_mean"] and c["status"] == "complete":
            pts[c["model"]].setdefault(c["width"], []).append((c["n"], c["pressure_l2_mean"], c["pressure_l2_seeds"])); params[c["model"]][c["width"]] = c["params"]
    return pts, params
def mid(a, b):
    return mpl.colors.to_hex((np.array(mpl.colors.to_rgb(a)) + np.array(mpl.colors.to_rgb(b))) / 2)
shades = {"isla": [BLUE_PALE, BLUE_LIGHT, BLUE], "gt": [RED_LIGHT, mid(RED_LIGHT, RED), RED]}
PANELS = (("drivaerml", "DrivAerML Surface task (48 validation cars)", [27, 54, 109, 218, 435], (22, 600), (0.030, 0.165), [0.04, 0.05, 0.07, 0.1, 0.15], SURF, 435),
          ("hilift", "HiLiftAeroML (180 validation wings)", [35, 210, 510, 1260], (28, 1560), (0.024, 0.17), [0.03, 0.04, 0.05, 0.07, 0.1, 0.15], HLS, 210))
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 1, figsize=(8.0, 9.2))
for ax, (ds, title, ticks, xlim, ylim, yticks, stand, nref) in zip(axes, PANELS):
    pts, params = grid(ds)
    nn = np.geomspace(xlim[0] * 1.08, xlim[1] * 0.95, 120)
    for m, key in (("isla", "isla_ref"), ("gt", "gt")):
        kw = series_kwargs(key); F = SLF[f"{ds}|{m}"]; f = F["fit"]; accepted = F["law_accepted_rms_below_3pct"]
        for shade, (w, rows) in zip(shades[m], sorted(pts[m].items())):
            rows = sorted(rows); x = [r[0] for r in rows]; y = [r[1] for r in rows]
            ax.plot(x, y, marker=kw["marker"], color=shade, mec=INK2, mew=0.4, ls="none", ms=6, label=f"{STYLE[key]['label']}, {w} wide")
            for r in rows:
                ax.plot([r[0]] * len(r[2]), r[2], ls="none", marker="_", color=shade, ms=7, mew=1.1)
            if accepted:
                ax.plot(nn, f["eps_inf"] + f["a"] * nn ** (-f["alpha"]) + f["b"] * params[m][w] ** (-f["beta"]), color=shade, ls=":", lw=1.1, zorder=0)
        if m == "isla" and accepted:
            ax.axhline(f["eps_inf"], color=BASELINE, ls="--", lw=0.8, zorder=0)
            ax.text(xlim[0] * 1.15, f["eps_inf"] * 0.985, f"ISLA's fitted floor {f['eps_inf']:.4f}", fontsize=7.5, color=INK2, va="top", ha="left")
    if stand.ds.fair_drive:
        for (a, key), dx in zip(REF_KEYS, (1.0, 1.12, 0.89)):
            star(ax, nref * dx, stand.err(a, "pressure_l2"), key, ms=13)
        ax.plot([], [], marker="*", ms=12, mfc="white", mec=INK, ls="none", label="reference configurations")
    ax.set_xscale("log"); ax.set_yscale("log"); ax.set_xticks(ticks); ax.set_xticklabels([f"{t:,}" for t in ticks])
    ax.set_yticks(yticks); ax.set_yticklabels([f"{t:.2f}" for t in yticks]); ax.yaxis.set_minor_formatter(mpl.ticker.NullFormatter()); ax.xaxis.set_minor_formatter(mpl.ticker.NullFormatter())
    ax.set_xlim(*xlim); ax.set_ylim(*ylim)
    ax.set_title(title, fontsize=9.5, loc="left")
    ax.set_xlabel("training cases [count]"); ax.set_ylabel("surface-pressure error,\narea-weighted relative L2 [–]")
    ax.legend(fontsize=7.4, ncol=2, loc="upper right")
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()
```

```{python}
print("Two readings of the curves come before any fit. The error is not one power law in the case count on either dataset: the local "
      "exponent (the negative log-log slope between adjacent rungs, @tbl-scaling-exponents) falls rung by rung, the signature of an approach "
      "to a floor. And parameters lower the curve at every rung without changing its slope much: the widest run improves on the narrowest "
      f"by up to {100 * max(max(gw[('drivaerml', m)].values()) for m in ('isla', 'gt')):.0f}% on the cars and up to "
      f"{100 * max(max(gw[('hilift', m)].values()) for m in ('isla', 'gt')):.0f}% on the wings, while a step from one rung to the next "
      "buys more than that below a few hundred cases.")
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-scaling-exponents
#| output: asis
def slope(rows, lo, hi):
    d = {r[0]: r[1] for r in rows}
    return -np.log(d[hi] / d[lo]) / np.log(hi / lo) if lo in d and hi in d else None
DS_NAME = {"drivaerml": "DrivAerML Surface", "hilift": "HiLiftAeroML"}
out = "| dataset | model | width | local exponent, rung to rung | widest ÷ narrowest error − 1, by rung |\n|---|---|--:|---|---|\n"
ratios = {}
for ds in ("drivaerml", "hilift"):
    pts, params = grid(ds)
    for m, name in (("isla", "ISLA"), ("gt", "GeoTransolver")):
        ws = sorted(pts[m]); rungs = sorted({r[0] for w in ws for r in pts[m][w]})
        ratios[(ds, m)] = params[m][ws[-1]] / params[m][ws[0]]
        for w in ws:
            rows = pts[m][w]
            cells = "; ".join(f"{a:,}→{b:,}: {s:.2f}" for a, b in zip(rungs, rungs[1:]) for s in [slope(rows, a, b)] if s is not None)
            gains = []
            for n in rungs:
                lo = {r[0]: r[1] for r in pts[m][ws[0]]}.get(n); hi = {r[0]: r[1] for r in pts[m][ws[-1]]}.get(n)
                gains.append(f"{n:,}: {100 * (hi / lo - 1):+.0f}%" if lo and hi else f"{n:,}: —")
            out += f"| {DS_NAME[ds]} | {name} | {w} | {cells} | {'; '.join(gains) if w == ws[0] else ''} |\n"
out += (f"\n: Local exponents of the error against training cases (the negative log-log slope between adjacent rungs, at each width) and the "
        f"change in error from the narrowest to the widest run at each rung (a {ratios[('drivaerml', 'isla')]:.0f}× parameter increase for ISLA "
        f"and {ratios[('drivaerml', 'gt')]:.0f}× for GeoTransolver). *Instrument:* as @fig-scaling-cases. How to read this: an exponent that falls "
        "with the rung is an approach to a floor, not a scale-free law; a positive change is a rung where the widest run is not the best. "
        "Data: results/scalelaw_2026-10-08.json.\n")
print(out)
```

### The fitted law {#sec-scaling-law}

**A floor plus two power laws reproduces every seed mean of ISLA to within a few percent on both
datasets; GeoTransolver's fit passes the same bar on the wings and misses it on the cars.** The form separates
three sources of error: what no amount of data or capacity removes, what more cases remove, and
what more parameters remove,

$$
\varepsilon(n, P) \;=\; \varepsilon_\infty \;+\; \underbrace{a\,n^{-\alpha}}_{D(n)} \;+\; \underbrace{b\,P^{-\beta}}_{\Pi(P)} ,
$$

with $n$ the training cases, $P$ the trainable parameters, $\varepsilon_\infty$ the floor, $D$
the data term and $\Pi$ the parameter term. The fit is least squares on the relative residual of
the seed means, with the floor bounded to at most 0.9 times the best measured error, a two-seed
bootstrap for the ranges, and acceptance when the RMS relative residual is below 3%, a bar set
before the fit. @tbl-scaling-fit gives the coefficients.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-scaling-fit
#| output: asis
out = ("| dataset | model | $\\varepsilon_\\infty$ | $a$ | $\\alpha$ | $b$ | $\\beta$ | RMS residual | accepted | "
       "crossover $n$ |\n|---|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|:--:|--:|\n")
UNIT = {"drivaerml": "cars", "hilift": "wings"}
for ds in ("drivaerml", "hilift"):
    for m, name in (("isla", "ISLA"), ("gt", "GeoTransolver")):
        F = SLF[f"{ds}|{m}"]; f = F["fit"]; b = F["bootstrap_p16_p50_p84"]
        rng_ = lambda k: f"{f[k]:.2f} ({b[k][0]:.2f} to {b[k][2]:.2f})"
        floor = f"{f['eps_inf']:.4f} ({b['eps_inf'][0]:.4f} to {b['eps_inf'][2]:.4f})" + (" (on its bound)" if f["eps_inf_on_bound"] else (" (zero)" if f["eps_inf"] < 1e-6 else ""))
        bval = f"{f['b']:.0f}" if f["b"] >= 10 else f"{f['b']:.2f}"
        out += f"| {DS_NAME[ds]} | {name} | {floor} | {f['a']:.1f} | {rng_('alpha')} | {bval} | {rng_('beta')} | {100 * f['rms_rel_residual']:.1f}% | {'yes' if F['law_accepted_rms_below_3pct'] else 'no'} | {F['n_star_recipe_width']:,.0f} {UNIT[ds]} |\n"
out += ("\n: The fitted law $\\varepsilon = \\varepsilon_\\infty + a\\,n^{-\\alpha} + b\\,P^{-\\beta}$ per architecture and dataset, 16th to 84th "
        "percentiles of a 400-draw two-seed bootstrap in parentheses; $D \\equiv a\\,n^{-\\alpha}$ is the data term and $\\Pi \\equiv b\\,P^{-\\beta}$ the "
        "parameter term. A fit is accepted when its RMS relative residual is below 3%. The last column, *crossover $n$*, "
        "is the case count at which $D = \\Pi$ at the narrowest width (ISLA 192, GeoTransolver 256), the crossover defined "
        "before the fit. *Instrument:* as @fig-scaling-cases. How to read this: GeoTransolver's DrivAerML row misses the bar and puts its floor on "
        "the bound, so its exponents are indicative. With three widths per model $\\beta$ is weakly identified (its bootstrap range says so); "
        "GeoTransolver's wing fit uses that freedom to set $\\beta$ near zero, which turns $b\\,P^{-\\beta}$ into a constant and sends "
        "$\\varepsilon_\\infty$ to zero, so its wing floor is carried by the parameter term. Data: results/scalelaw_2026-10-08.json.\n")
print(out)
```

```{python}
#| label: para-scaling-reading
#| output: asis
Dd = {m: SLF[f"drivaerml|{m}"] for m in ("isla", "gt")}; H = {m: SLF[f"hilift|{m}"] for m in ("isla", "gt")}
gt27 = SLF["drivaerml|gt"]["rungs_where_widest_is_not_best"][0]["by_width"]
print(f"For ISLA on the cars the floor lands inside its allowed range at {Dd['isla']['fit']['eps_inf']:.4f}, and the law reproduces the fifteen "
      f"seed means to {100 * Dd['isla']['fit']['rms_rel_residual']:.1f}% RMS. For GeoTransolver on the cars it misses the bar "
      f"({100 * Dd['gt']['fit']['rms_rel_residual']:.1f}%). The cause is its 27-car rung, where the 1,024-wide model "
      f"({gt27['1024']:.4f}) is worse than the 512-wide one ({gt27['512']:.4f}): an additive law has no term for a wide model losing to a "
      "narrower one at small data. "
      f"On the wings, where both fits pass, the data exponents are {H['isla']['fit']['alpha']:.2f} for ISLA and {H['gt']['fit']['alpha']:.2f} "
      "for GeoTransolver, inside each other's bootstrap range, although GeoTransolver's fit there sets its parameter term near a constant "
      f"($\\beta$ = {H['gt']['fit']['beta']:.2f}, floor {H['gt']['fit']['eps_inf']:.3f}). On the cars they are {Dd['isla']['fit']['alpha']:.2f} "
      f"and {Dd['gt']['fit']['alpha']:.2f}, an indicative agreement only, since GeoTransolver's fit misses the bar. **Where both fits pass, the two "
      "architectures convert cases into accuracy at the same rate; the rate differs between the datasets.** The exponents describe the reducible "
      "error above the floor, which is why $\\alpha$ exceeds every local slope of the total error in @tbl-scaling-exponents.")
```

### Compute allocation as a constrained minimization {#sec-iso-compute}

**Minimizing the fitted law over cases and parameters at fixed training compute gives a closed
form: the optimal path keeps the data term a fixed fraction $\beta/\alpha$ of the parameter term,
and grows parameters as $C^{\alpha/(\alpha+\beta)}$ and cases as $C^{\beta/(\alpha+\beta)}$.**
Picture the plane of training cases against parameters (@fig-iso-compute). The fitted error is a
landscape on it, falling toward the upper right. A training budget is a curve on the same plane:
each case is seen for the same number of epochs at the same cell count, and the arithmetic of a
step grows with the parameters it multiplies, so compute is proportional to $P\,n$ and a fixed
budget is a straight line of slope −1 in log-log axes. The best model for that budget is where the
budget line touches the lowest error contour.

```{python}
#| label: setup-iso
#| include: false
FI = SLF["drivaerml|isla"]["fit"]
a_, al_, b_, be_, e_ = FI["a"], FI["alpha"], FI["b"], FI["beta"], FI["eps_inf"]
law = lambda n, P: e_ + a_ * n ** (-al_) + b_ * P ** (-be_)
Kp = (be_ * b_ / (al_ * a_)) ** (1 / be_)                        # optimal path: P = Kp * n**(alpha/beta)
path_P = lambda n: Kp * n ** (al_ / be_)
P_REF, N_REF = COST["DrivAerML Surface"]["ISLA"]["n_parameters"], 435
C_REF = P_REF * N_REF
n_opt = (C_REF / Kp) ** (be_ / (al_ + be_)); P_opt = C_REF / n_opt
pts_sl, params_sl = grid("drivaerml")
P_lo, P_hi = min(params_sl["isla"].values()), max(params_sl["isla"].values())
n_lo, n_hi = 27, 435
n_on_path = lambda P: (P / Kp) ** (be_ / al_)
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-iso-compute
#| fig-cap: >
#|   The fitted law of ISLA on the DrivAerML Surface task (@tbl-scaling-fit) as a landscape over
#|   training cases and parameters: filled contours and labeled isolines of the predicted
#|   surface-pressure error. Dashed white diagonals: budgets of equal training compute, proportional to
#|   parameters × cases, labeled as multiples of the reference ISLA's (its parameters at 435 cars).
#|   Black line: the compute-optimal path, where each budget line touches its lowest contour.
#|   Small white circles: the fifteen runs the law is fitted to; the colors are full inside the
#|   dashed rectangle they span and faint outside it, where the contours are extrapolation. Blue star: the reference ISLA, a
#|   different instrument whose measured error is printed beside it. *Instrument:* as
#|   @fig-scaling-cases. How to read this: moving along a dashed line spends the same compute; the
#|   best point on it is where it crosses the black path. The figure assumes compute ∝ P·n, which
#|   counts arithmetic, not GPU wall time (see the callout below). Data: results/scalelaw_2026-10-08.json.
#| fig-alt: "Contour map of predicted error over training cases on the x axis and parameters on the y axis, both logarithmic, with diagonal iso-compute lines, a steep black optimal path, the fitted runs as white dots inside a clear rectangle and a blue star for the reference ISLA."
nn = np.geomspace(15, 2500, 220); PP = np.geomspace(3e6, 1.2e9, 220)
NN, PG = np.meshgrid(nn, PP); EE = law(NN, PG)
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8.0, 6.4))
levels = [0.037, 0.038, 0.039, 0.040, 0.042, 0.045, 0.050, 0.060, 0.080, 0.120]
bounds = [e_] + levels + [0.4]
norm = mpl.colors.BoundaryNorm(bounds, 256)
inside = (NN >= n_lo) & (NN <= n_hi) & (PG >= P_lo) & (PG <= P_hi)
ax.contourf(NN, PG, EE, levels=bounds, cmap="viridis", norm=norm, alpha=0.35)                  # extrapolation: faint
cf = ax.contourf(NN, PG, np.where(inside, EE, np.nan), levels=bounds, cmap="viridis", norm=norm, alpha=0.9)  # the fitted range: full
cs = ax.contour(NN, PG, EE, levels=levels, colors=INK2, linewidths=0.7)
ax.clabel(cs, fmt=lambda v: f"{v:.3f}", fontsize=7.5, inline=True)
from matplotlib.patches import Rectangle
ax.add_patch(Rectangle((n_lo, P_lo), n_hi - n_lo, P_hi - P_lo, fc="none", ec=INK, lw=1.0, ls="--", zorder=4))
for k in (0.01, 0.1, 1, 10, 100):
    ax.plot(nn, k * C_REF / nn, color=WHITE, lw=1.2, ls=(0, (4, 3)), zorder=4)
    xl = 0.6 * np.sqrt(k * C_REF * np.sqrt(nn[0] * nn[-1]) / np.sqrt(PP[0] * PP[-1])); yl = k * C_REF / xl
    if PP[0] < yl < PP[-1]:
        ax.text(xl, yl, f" {k:g}× ", fontsize=7.8, color=INK, rotation=-36, ha="center", va="center", path_effects=halo(), zorder=5)
ax.plot(nn, path_P(nn), color=INK, lw=2.0, zorder=5, label="compute-optimal path")
for w, rows in pts_sl["isla"].items():
    for r in rows:
        ax.plot(r[0], params_sl["isla"][w], marker="o", ms=5, mfc="white", mec=INK, mew=0.8, ls="none", zorder=6)
star(ax, N_REF, P_REF, "isla_ref", ms=18)
ax.annotate(f"reference ISLA\nmeasured {SURF.err('ISLA', 'pressure_l2'):.4f}\nlaw {law(N_REF, P_REF):.4f}", (N_REF, P_REF),
            textcoords="offset points", xytext=(12, -6), fontsize=8, color=BLUE, zorder=7, va="top",
            bbox=dict(boxstyle="round,pad=0.25", fc="white", ec="none", alpha=0.9))
ax.plot([n_opt], [P_opt], marker="D", ms=7, mfc=WHITE, mec=INK, mew=1.4, zorder=7)
ax.annotate(f"optimum for the\nreference budget:\n{n_opt:.0f} cases, {P_opt / 1e6:.0f}M\nlaw {law(n_opt, P_opt):.4f}", (n_opt, P_opt),
            textcoords="offset points", xytext=(10, -22), ha="left", va="top", fontsize=8, color=INK, path_effects=halo(), zorder=7)
ax.set_xscale("log"); ax.set_yscale("log"); ax.set_xlim(nn[0], nn[-1]); ax.set_ylim(PP[0], PP[-1])
ax.set_xticks([20, 50, 100, 200, 500, 1000, 2000]); ax.set_xticklabels(["20", "50", "100", "200", "500", "1,000", "2,000"])
ax.set_yticks([5e6, 1e7, 2e7, 5e7, 1e8, 2e8, 5e8, 1e9]); ax.set_yticklabels(["5M", "10M", "20M", "50M", "100M", "200M", "500M", "1B"])
ax.xaxis.set_minor_formatter(mpl.ticker.NullFormatter()); ax.yaxis.set_minor_formatter(mpl.ticker.NullFormatter()); ax.grid(False)
ax.set_xlabel("training cases $n$ [count]"); ax.set_ylabel("trainable parameters $P$ [count]")
cb = fig.colorbar(cf, ax=ax, pad=0.02, shrink=0.85, ticks=[0.037, 0.040, 0.045, 0.060, 0.120], format="%.3f")
cb.set_label("predicted surface-pressure error [–]")
ax.legend(loc="lower right", fontsize=8.2)
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()
```

The figure has a closed form. Minimize the law over $(n, P)$ subject to the budget $P\,n = C$:

$$
\min_{n,\,P}\; a\,n^{-\alpha} + b\,P^{-\beta}
\quad\text{s.t.}\quad \log n + \log P = \log C .
$$

The floor drops out because it does not depend on either variable. In the logarithmic variables
the objective is convex and the constraint is linear, so the stationarity condition of the
Lagrangian is sufficient. It reads $\partial\varepsilon/\partial\log n = \partial\varepsilon/\partial\log P$:

$$
\alpha\, D(n^\ast) \;=\; \beta\, \Pi(P^\ast),
\qquad
P^\ast \propto C^{\alpha/(\alpha+\beta)},
\qquad
n^\ast \propto C^{\beta/(\alpha+\beta)} .
$$

In words: at the optimum, the last dollar spent on cases and the last dollar spent on parameters
buy the same reduction of error. Because $\alpha > \beta$, the data term decays faster, so the
optimum keeps it the smaller of the two, at the fixed fraction $\beta/\alpha$ of the parameter
term, and puts most of each new order of magnitude of compute into parameters.

```{python}
#| label: para-iso-numbers
#| output: asis
n192 = n_on_path(min(params_sl["isla"].values())); n_eq = SLF["drivaerml|isla"]["n_star_recipe_width"]
P435 = path_P(435)
print(f"With ISLA's exponents on the cars ($\\alpha$ = {al_:.2f}, $\\beta$ = {be_:.2f}) the path grows parameters as "
      f"$C^{{{al_ / (al_ + be_):.2f}}}$ and cases as $C^{{{be_ / (al_ + be_):.2f}}}$: a tenfold budget buys {10 ** (al_ / (al_ + be_)):.1f}× the "
      f"parameters and {10 ** (be_ / (al_ + be_)):.1f}× the cases, and the data term sits at {be_ / al_:.2f} of the parameter term all along it. "
      f"Two numbers locate the path on the measured grid. At ISLA's narrowest width ({min(params_sl['isla'].values()) / 1e6:.1f}M parameters) the "
      f"optimal case count is {n192:.0f} cars, about twice the {n_eq:.0f} cars at which the two terms are equal (the crossover of "
      "@tbl-scaling-fit, which marks where the terms trade places, not where the budget is best spent). At the full 435-car training set the "
      f"optimal model has {P435 / 1e6:.0f}M parameters. The reference ISLA, at {P_REF / 1e6:.1f}M parameters and 435 cars, lies above the path: "
      f"for its compute the law prefers {n_opt:.0f} cars and {P_opt / 1e6:.0f}M parameters and predicts {law(n_opt, P_opt):.4f} there against "
      f"{law(N_REF, P_REF):.4f} at the reference point. The minimum is shallow, and DrivAerML has no more cars to buy. The path counts "
      "arithmetic, a step's cost in proportion to $P\\,n$; on a GPU, widening a narrow ISLA is nearly free in wall time while depth is paid "
      "in full, so the wall-clock optimum leans further toward width than the figure shows (the callout below measures it).")
```

**When the data are capped, the problem has a corner solution.** In engineering a training case is
a CFD solution, and its cost is in solver hours, not GPU hours; a dataset of 435 cars is what
exists. With $n$ fixed at $n_\text{max}$ the only remaining variable is $P$, the error falls
monotonically toward $\varepsilon_\infty + a\,n_\text{max}^{-\alpha}$, and every further unit of
compute goes to parameters at a diminishing rate $\beta\,\Pi(P)$ per $e$-fold. That is the regime
the reference configurations live in on every dataset of this book. The law then answers a
different question: what one more simulated case is worth. At the reference ISLA, the marginal
gains per $e$-fold are:

```{python}
#| label: para-marginal
#| output: asis
Dn, Pi = a_ * N_REF ** (-al_), b_ * P_REF ** (-be_)
print(f"- **cases**: $\\alpha D$ = {al_ * Dn:.4f} of error per $e$-fold, a doubling of the car count worth {100 * al_ * Dn * np.log(2) / law(N_REF, P_REF):.1f}% of the predicted error;")
print(f"- **parameters**: $\\beta \\Pi$ = {be_ * Pi:.4f} per $e$-fold, a doubling of the parameters worth {100 * be_ * Pi * np.log(2) / law(N_REF, P_REF):.1f}%.")
print()
print(f"The floor of the law, {e_:.4f}, is the error no amount of either buys at this cell count, this instrument and this metric.")
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Optional: when a step's cost is not proportional to its parameters"}
The budget $C \propto P\,n$ counts arithmetic: the 6 floating-point operations per parameter per
token of a forward and backward pass through a linear map. On a GPU a step's wall time is not
proportional to $P$ when the network is too narrow to fill the device or when memory traffic, not
arithmetic, sets the pace. Write the per-case cost as $k\,P^\gamma$, so the budget is $n\,k\,P^\gamma
= C$. The same Lagrangian gives

$$
\alpha\gamma\, D(n^\ast) = \beta\, \Pi(P^\ast), \qquad
P^\ast \propto C^{\alpha/(\alpha\gamma+\beta)}, \qquad
n^\ast \propto C^{\beta/(\alpha\gamma+\beta)} .
$$

A $\gamma$ below one makes parameters cheaper than arithmetic suggests and tilts the path toward
width. The one-GPU cost sweep (@sec-cost-sweep) measures $\gamma$ directly:

```{python}
#| label: para-gamma
#| output: asis
s192, s384, s384d = (at(a, 200000) for a in ("isla_192x12_cos_fused", "isla_ref_r1_384x12_cos_fused", "isla_ref_r2_384x24_cos_fused"))
gam = lambda r0, r1: np.log(st.median(r1["step_ms"]) / st.median(r0["step_ms"])) / np.log(r1["n_params"] / r0["n_params"])
print(f"at 200,000 tokens, widening ISLA from 192 to 384 (12 layers) multiplies the parameters by {s384['n_params'] / s192['n_params']:.1f} "
      f"and the step time by {st.median(s384['step_ms']) / st.median(s192['step_ms']):.2f}, so $\\gamma \\approx$ {gam(s192, s384):.2f} along width; "
      f"deepening 384 wide from 12 to 24 layers gives $\\gamma \\approx$ {gam(s384, s384d):.2f} along depth. Width below 384 is nearly free in "
      "wall time on this device and depth is paid in full; the path of @fig-iso-compute is the arithmetic one. Data: "
      "results/cost_sweep_ref_gb300_bf16_2026-09-22.json.")
```
:::

### The exponents belong to the dataset {#sec-exponents-datasets}

**The rate at which error falls with cases is a property of the dataset and the task, and it does
not transfer between them.** The fitted data exponent of ISLA is
`{python} f"{SLF['drivaerml|isla']['fit']['alpha']:.2f}"` on the cars and
`{python} f"{SLF['hilift|isla']['fit']['alpha']:.2f}"` on the wings. GeoTransolver's sits within
the bootstrap spread of ISLA's on the wings, where both fits pass their bar, and close to it on the
cars, where GeoTransolver's fit misses the bar. A compute-allocation rule measured on one dataset
therefore says nothing quantitative about another, and a claim that one architecture "scales
better" needs both architectures' exponents on the same ladder. @fig-exponents-datasets compares the learning-curve
exponent of the total error, the single slope of a least-squares line in log-log axes, for the two
architectures on every dataset whose ladder this book can read.

```{python}
#| label: fig-exponents-datasets
#| fig-cap: >
#|   Learning-curve exponents of the total error against training cases, the negative slope of a
#|   least-squares line through the seed means in log-log axes, for ISLA (squares) and
#|   GeoTransolver (circles) over the rungs named on the left; the gray bar joins the pair.
#|   *Instrument:* ISLA at 384 wide, 256 slices, 5e-4, raw slice reads (@sec-study-configurations),
#|   against GeoTransolver at 512 wide (3e-3 on the surfaces, 1e-3 on the lug); DrivAerML and
#|   HiLiftAeroML at 100,000 training cells, the lug with every node queried. How to read this: a
#|   point further right falls faster with data. The exponents are of the total error, so a shared
#|   floor lowers both, and they sit below the fitted $\alpha$ of the reducible error
#|   (@tbl-scaling-fit). An exponent says how a gap moves with data, not where it sits. Data:
#|   results/scalelaw_2026-10-08.json, results/solids_lug_2026-09-22.json.
#| fig-alt: "Dumbbell plot of learning-curve exponents for ISLA and GeoTransolver on three datasets."
LUGX = J("solids_lug_2026-09-22.json")["learning_curve_exponents"]
def total_slope(ds, m, w):
    rows = sorted(grid(ds)[0][m][w]); x = np.log([r[0] for r in rows]); y = np.log([r[1] for r in rows])
    return -np.polyfit(x, y, 1)[0]
ROWS = [("DrivAerML Surface, pressure,\n27 to 435 cars", total_slope("drivaerml", "isla", 384), total_slope("drivaerml", "gt", 512)),
        ("HiLiftAeroML, pressure,\n35 to 1,260 wings", total_slope("hilift", "isla", 384), total_slope("hilift", "gt", 512)),
        ("GINOT lug, von Mises stress,\n300 to 2,400 lugs", LUGX["isla_r1"]["exponent"], LUGX["gt512"]["exponent"])]
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.6, 0.62 * len(ROWS) + 1.4))
ys = np.arange(len(ROWS))[::-1]
for y, (lab, a_i, a_g) in zip(ys, ROWS):
    ax.plot([a_g, a_i], [y, y], color=BASELINE, lw=2.4, zorder=1)
    ax.plot([a_i], [y], **series_kwargs("isla_ref", ls="none", ms=8), zorder=3)
    ax.plot([a_g], [y], **series_kwargs("gt", ls="none", ms=8), zorder=3)
    for v, key in ((a_i, "isla_ref"), (a_g, "gt")):
        ax.annotate(f"{v:.2f}", (v, y), textcoords="offset points", xytext=(0, 8), ha="center", fontsize=8, color=STYLE[key]["color"], path_effects=halo())
ax.set_yticks(ys); ax.set_yticklabels([r[0] for r in ROWS], fontsize=8.5); ax.grid(False, axis="y")
ax.set_xlabel("learning-curve exponent of the total error [–]   (error ∝ cases$^{-\\mathrm{exponent}}$)")
ax.set_xlim(max(0, min(min(r[1], r[2]) for r in ROWS) - 0.12), max(max(r[1], r[2]) for r in ROWS) + 0.12); ax.set_ylim(-0.6, len(ROWS) - 0.2)
from matplotlib.lines import Line2D
ax.legend(handles=[Line2D([], [], **series_kwargs("isla_ref", ls="none")), Line2D([], [], **series_kwargs("gt", ls="none"))],
          loc="lower left", fontsize=8.2)
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()
```

```{python}
#| label: para-exponents-datasets
#| output: asis
steeper = [r[0].split(",")[0] for r in ROWS if r[1] > 1.05 * r[2]]
print(f"ISLA's total error falls faster with data than GeoTransolver's on {len(steeper)} of the {len(ROWS)} ladders "
      f"({', '.join(steeper)}). On the wings that is not a different rate: the fitted exponents of the reducible error agree there "
      "(@tbl-scaling-fit), and on the cars, where GeoTransolver's fit misses its bar, they agree only indicatively. ISLA's data coefficient $a$ is the larger, so it starts from a higher error at "
      "the smallest rung and closes the distance by the full training set. A steeper total-error curve can mean a faster rate or a larger "
      "coefficient at the same rate, and only the fitted law separates the two. Where the curves end is what the reference standings "
      "measure (@sec-standing).")
```

## Cost {#sec-cost-sweep}

**Above 100,000 tokens per case the time and memory of a training step grow linearly in the
number of tokens for every architecture, with no quadratic term up to 600,000; below about 40,000
tokens the step is launch-bound and nearly flat.** A *token* is one sampled cell the model
processes in a step. Slice attention costs $\mathcal{O}(N M)$ in the $N$ tokens and $M$ slices,
never $\mathcal{O}(N^2)$ (@sec-isla-slices), so the linear growth is what the construction
predicts. *Launch-bound* means the GPU spends the step waiting for its next small kernel to be
dispatched by the CPU, so the step time is a fixed overhead per kernel and does not depend on how
much data each kernel handles. The memory reported is the allocator peak of @sec-review-frontier,
the largest total size of live tensors during the step.

@fig-cost-sweep sweeps the token count from 2,500 to 600,000 on one GPU for five configurations
and adds the reference configurations' training peaks.

```{python}
#| label: fig-cost-sweep
#| fig-cap: >
#|   Training-step time (top) and allocator peak memory (bottom) against tokens per case, 2,500 to
#|   600,000, on one GB300 with bfloat16 autocast, a batch of one case, the optimizer step
#|   included, every model compiled and ISLA with the fused geometry kernel; median of ten
#|   measured steps after warm-up on random inputs. Lines: ISLA at 192 and 384 wide (12 layers);
#|   GeoTransolver at 256 wide (its reference width) and 512 wide; Transolver at 256 wide.
#|   *Instrument:* ISLA at 192 and 384 wide, 256 slices (@sec-study-configurations); no training
#|   is involved, so the slice reads and the rate do not enter. Black-edged stars (bottom): the

#|   the lines are joined measurements, not fits; a slope of one decade per decade is linear cost.
#|   The panel ranks per-step cost; it does not give wall-clock training time, which includes data
#|   loading (@tbl-ref-cost). Data: results/cost_sweep_ref_gb300_bf16_2026-09-22.json.
#| fig-alt: "Two stacked log-log panels against tokens per case from 2,500 to 600,000: step time flat below about 40,000 tokens then rising linearly, and peak memory rising linearly throughout, five lines each, with three stars for the reference configurations on the memory panel."
COST_ARMS = [("isla_ref_r1_384x12_cos_fused", "isla_ref", "ISLA, 384 × 12", dict(color=BLUE, ls="-")),
             ("isla_192x12_cos_fused", "isla_ref", "ISLA, 192 × 12", dict(color=BLUE_LIGHT, ls="-")),
             ("geotransolver_256", "gt", "GeoTransolver, 256", dict(color=RED, ls="-")),
             ("geotransolver_512", "gt", "GeoTransolver, 512", dict(color=RED_LIGHT, ls="-")),
             ("transolver_256", "t", "Transolver, 256", {})]
fig, (ax0, ax1) = plt.subplots(2, 1, figsize=(8.0, 7.4), sharex=True, gridspec_kw=dict(hspace=0.08))
for arm, key, lab, ov in COST_ARMS:
    rows = sorted([r for r in CS if r["arm"] == arm and r["status"] == "ok"], key=lambda r: r["tokens"])
    xs = [r["tokens"] for r in rows]

    ax1.plot(xs, [r["peak_allocated_gib"] for r in rows], **series_kwargs(key, label=lab, ms=5, **ov))
TOK = {"ISLA": 200000, "GeoTransolver": 200000, "Transolver": 100000}
for a, key in REF_KEYS:
    star(ax1, TOK[a] * {"ISLA": 0.93, "GeoTransolver": 1.07, "Transolver": 1.0}[a], COST["DrivAerML Surface"][a]["peak_gib"], key, ms=15)
ax1.plot([], [], marker="*", ms=12, mfc="white", mec=INK, ls="none", label="reference configurations, training peak")

    ax.axvspan(2000, 40000, color=PAPER, zorder=0)
ax0.text(9500, 300, "launch-bound below\nabout 40,000 tokens", fontsize=8.5, color=INK2, ha="center", va="center", path_effects=halo())
ax0.set_ylabel("training step [ms]"); ax1.set_ylabel("allocator peak [GiB]")
ax0.set_yticks([20, 50, 100, 200, 500]); ax0.set_yticklabels(["20", "50", "100", "200", "500"])
ax1.set_yticks([0.5, 1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 50, 100, 200]); ax1.set_yticklabels(["0.5", "1", "2", "5", "10", "20", "50", "100", "200"])
ax1.set_xlim(2000, 800000)
ax1.set_xticks([2500, 10000, 40000, 100000, 200000, 600000]); ax1.set_xticklabels(["2,500", "10,000", "40,000", "100,000", "200,000", "600,000"])

    ax.xaxis.set_minor_formatter(mpl.ticker.NullFormatter()); ax.yaxis.set_minor_formatter(mpl.ticker.NullFormatter())
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-cost-slopes
#| output: asis
out = "| configuration | parameters | step per 100,000 tokens [ms] | memory per 100,000 tokens [GiB] | largest residual of the linear fit, step / memory |\n|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|\n"
for arm, key, lab, _ in COST_ARMS:
    rows = sorted([r for r in CS if r["arm"] == arm and r["status"] == "ok" and r["tokens"] >= 100000], key=lambda r: r["tokens"])
    x = np.array([r["tokens"] for r in rows]) / 1e5
    t = np.array([st.median(r["step_ms"]) for r in rows]); m = np.array([r["peak_allocated_gib"] for r in rows])
    kt, ct = np.polyfit(x, t, 1); km, cm = np.polyfit(x, m, 1)
    rt = np.max(np.abs((kt * x + ct) / t - 1)); rm = np.max(np.abs((km * x + cm) / m - 1))
    out += f"| {lab} | {rows[0]['n_params'] / 1e6:.1f}M | {kt:.0f} | {km:.1f} | {100 * rt:.1f}% / {100 * rm:.1f}% |\n"
print(out)
print(": The per-token cost above 100,000 tokens: the slope of a straight line fitted to step time and to allocator peak over the measured counts "
      "from 100,000 to 600,000, and the largest relative deviation of any measured point from that line. *Instrument:* as @fig-cost-sweep. "
      "How to read this: residuals of a few percent over a sixfold range of tokens leave no room for a quadratic term; the slopes rank what a "
      "token costs each configuration on one GPU, not what a training run costs. Data: results/cost_sweep_ref_gb300_bf16_2026-09-22.json.")
```

```{python}
#| label: para-cost
#| output: asis
r = lambda arm, tok: at(arm, tok)
flat = st.median(r("isla_ref_r1_384x12_cos_fused", 40000)["step_ms"]) / st.median(r("isla_ref_r1_384x12_cos_fused", 2500)["step_ms"])
g = r("geotransolver_256", 200000)
print(f"Three readings follow. In the launch-bound regime a sixteenfold increase in tokens, 2,500 to 40,000, moves ISLA's step by a factor of "
      f"{flat:.2f}: a small case costs nearly as much per step as a medium one, and ISLA and GeoTransolver cost the same there. Above "
      "100,000 tokens the slopes of @tbl-cost-slopes rank the configurations per token, "
      "and ISLA at 192 wide is the cheapest after Transolver. Memory is where the architectures differ most: at 200,000 tokens GeoTransolver "
      f"at its reference width reserves {g['reserved_bytes'] / 2**30:.0f} GiB in the allocator's cache for an allocator peak of "
      f"{g['peak_allocated_gib']:.0f} GiB, so the card it needs is set by its reserve, not by its live tensors. Its training peak on real "
      f"DrivAerML cars at the same width and token count is {COST['DrivAerML Surface']['GeoTransolver']['peak_gib']:.0f} GiB (@tbl-ref-cost); the "
      "sweep runs random inputs on one GPU, and the difference between the two is not attributed.")
```

<!-- SLOT: per-token step time and memory at the reference configurations (fig-cost-sweep-ref) -->

::: {.callout-tip title="Choosing a token budget"}
Train at 100,000 to 200,000 cells per case: the error has saturated (@tbl-cells-ladder) and the
step is in the linear regime, so the token budget sets memory and time in proportion. Below
40,000 tokens a step costs nearly as much as at 40,000, and below 100,000 cells ISLA pays the
quadrature-noise penalty of @sec-deficit-anatomy; if a small budget is forced, score with the
stratified sampler (@sec-using-sampler).
:::
